title: [Contract] Implement stream creation with token escrow
body:
## Summary
Implement the `create_stream` entry point on the Soroban smart contract. When called, the contract must transfer the full stream amount from the sender into escrow (the contract's own address) and persist a `Stream` struct in contract storage.

## Implementation Steps
1. Define a `Stream` struct with fields: `sender`, `recipient`, `token`, `rate_per_second`, `start_time`, `end_time`, `withdrawn`.
2. Define a `DataKey` enum with variants `Stream(u64)` and `NextId`.
3. In `create_stream`, validate that `end_time > start_time` and `rate_per_second > 0`.
4. Compute `total = rate_per_second * (end_time - start_time)` and call `token::Client::transfer` to move funds into escrow.
5. Persist the stream under `DataKey::Stream(next_id)` using `env.storage().persistent()`.
6. Increment and persist `NextId`.
7. Return the new stream ID.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] `create_stream` compiles to WASM without warnings.
- [ ] Unit test verifies that the contract holds the correct token balance after creation.
- [ ] Unit test verifies that an invalid time range panics with a descriptive message.
- [ ] `cargo clippy -- -D warnings` passes.

title: [Contract] Implement time-based withdrawal logic
body:
## Summary
Implement the `withdraw` entry point that allows the stream recipient to claim tokens proportional to elapsed time.

## Implementation Steps
1. Load the `Stream` from persistent storage; panic with `"stream not found"` if absent.
2. Require auth from `stream.recipient`.
3. Compute `now = min(env.ledger().timestamp(), stream.end_time)`.
4. Compute `vested = rate_per_second * (now - start_time)`.
5. Compute `available = vested - stream.withdrawn`; assert `available > 0`.
6. Update `stream.withdrawn += available` and re-persist.
7. Transfer `available` tokens from the contract to the recipient.
8. Return the withdrawn amount.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] Unit test: recipient withdraws correct amount at the midpoint of a stream.
- [ ] Unit test: calling `withdraw` twice in the same ledger timestamp yields 0 on the second call (or panics).
- [ ] Unit test: withdrawal after `end_time` is capped at the total stream value.
- [ ] `cargo test` passes.

title: [Contract] Implement stream cancellation with pro-rata refund
body:
## Summary
Implement `cancel_stream` so the sender can terminate a stream early. Vested tokens go to the recipient; unvested tokens are refunded to the sender.

## Implementation Steps
1. Load the stream; require auth from `stream.sender`.
2. Compute vested amount at the current ledger timestamp (same formula as `withdraw`).
3. Subtract already-withdrawn amount to get `recipient_due`.
4. Compute `sender_refund = total - vested`.
5. Transfer `recipient_due` to recipient (if > 0) and `sender_refund` to sender (if > 0).
6. Remove the stream from storage with `env.storage().persistent().remove(...)`.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] Unit test: cancel at 30 % elapsed — recipient receives 30 %, sender receives 70 %.
- [ ] Unit test: cancel after `end_time` — sender receives 0 refund.
- [ ] Unit test: only the sender can cancel (non-sender auth attempt panics).
- [ ] `cargo test` passes.

title: [Frontend] Build active streams dashboard
body:
## Summary
Create the main dashboard view that lists all active payment streams for the connected wallet.

## Implementation Steps
1. Create a `StreamList` component that accepts a `streams: Stream[]` prop.
2. For each stream render a card showing: stream ID, sender, recipient, token symbol, rate per second, and a live progress bar (elapsed / total duration).
3. Use Radix UI `Card` or a plain `div` with accessible roles.
4. Show an empty-state illustration and message when `streams.length === 0`.
5. Wire the component into `App.tsx`.
6. Add a `useStreams` hook stub that will later fetch from the contract; for now return mock data.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] `StreamList` renders without console errors.
- [ ] Empty state is visible when no streams are passed.
- [ ] Component test using `@testing-library/react` asserts card count matches mock data length.
- [ ] Accessible: each card has an `aria-label` describing the stream.

title: [Frontend] Implement "Create Stream" form with validation
body:
## Summary
Add a modal form that lets users create a new payment stream by filling in recipient address, token, rate, start time, and end time.

## Implementation Steps
1. Use Radix UI `Dialog` for the modal shell.
2. Build a controlled form with fields: `recipient` (text), `token` (select), `ratePerSecond` (number), `startTime` (datetime-local), `endTime` (datetime-local).
3. Validate on submit: recipient must be a valid Stellar address (56-char G… string), `endTime > startTime`, `ratePerSecond > 0`.
4. Display inline field-level error messages using `aria-describedby`.
5. On valid submit, call a `createStream(params)` service function (stub for now) and close the dialog.
6. Show a Radix UI `Toast` on success.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] Form renders inside a Radix Dialog.
- [ ] Submitting with invalid data shows error messages without closing the dialog.
- [ ] Submitting with valid data calls the stub service and shows a success toast.
- [ ] Component test covers the validation error paths.

title: [Frontend] Add "Cancel Stream" button with confirmation state
body:
## Summary
Add a cancel action to each stream card that requires a two-step confirmation before invoking the contract.

## Implementation Steps
1. Add a `CancelButton` component that starts in an idle state showing "Cancel Stream".
2. On first click, transition to a confirmation state: replace the button text with "Confirm Cancel" and show a secondary "Keep Stream" button.
3. On "Confirm Cancel", call `cancelStream(streamId)` service stub and optimistically remove the stream from local state.
4. On "Keep Stream" or focus-loss, revert to idle state.
5. While the cancellation is in-flight, disable both buttons and show a spinner.
6. On error, show a Radix UI `Toast` with the error message and revert state.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] Button cycles through idle → confirm → loading → (success | error) states.
- [ ] Component test asserts that the confirmation step appears after the first click.
- [ ] Component test asserts that "Keep Stream" reverts to idle without calling the service.
- [ ] No state leaks between different stream cards.

title: [Frontend] Wallet connection and Freighter integration
body:
## Summary
Integrate the Freighter browser wallet so users can connect their Stellar account and sign transactions.

## Implementation Steps
1. Install `@stellar/freighter-api` (exact version pin).
2. Create a `useWallet` hook that exposes `{ publicKey, connect, disconnect, isConnected }`.
3. On `connect`, call `freighter.getPublicKey()` and store in React state.
4. Render a "Connect Wallet" button in the header when disconnected; show a truncated public key and "Disconnect" when connected.
5. Gate the "Create Stream" dialog behind wallet connection.
6. Pass the `publicKey` to `useStreams` so it can filter streams by sender/recipient.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] `useWallet` hook is unit-tested with a mocked Freighter API.
- [ ] Header shows correct connected/disconnected states.
- [ ] "Create Stream" button is disabled and shows a tooltip when wallet is not connected.
- [ ] No Freighter API calls are made during unit tests (mock is injected).

title: [Testing] Integration test: stream creation and full lifecycle
body:
## Summary
Write an end-to-end integration test that deploys the contract to a local Soroban sandbox and exercises the full stream lifecycle: create → withdraw → cancel.

## Implementation Steps
1. Use `soroban-cli` sandbox or the JS `@stellar/stellar-sdk` `SorobanRpc` client pointed at a local node.
2. Deploy the compiled WASM and capture the contract address.
3. Mint test tokens to a sender account.
4. Call `create_stream` and assert the contract holds the correct token balance.
5. Advance ledger time by 50 % of the stream duration.
6. Call `withdraw` and assert the recipient received 50 % of the total.
7. Advance to 75 % and call `cancel_stream`; assert sender receives 25 % refund and recipient receives the remaining 25 %.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] Test runs with `npm test` in `tests/integration`.
- [ ] All assertions pass against a fresh sandbox.
- [ ] Test cleans up (removes deployed contract) after completion.
- [ ] CI workflow runs this job and fails the build on assertion errors.

title: [Testing] Integration test: stream depletion and over-withdrawal guard
body:
## Summary
Verify that a fully depleted stream cannot be over-withdrawn and that the contract state is consistent after the stream ends.

## Implementation Steps
1. Create a stream with a short duration (e.g., 100 seconds).
2. Advance ledger time past `end_time`.
3. Call `withdraw` and assert the full stream amount is transferred.
4. Attempt a second `withdraw` call and assert it fails with a descriptive error (not a silent no-op).
5. Assert the contract's token balance is 0 after full depletion.
6. Assert `get_stream` still returns the stream record with `withdrawn == total`.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] Test covers the post-`end_time` withdrawal cap.
- [ ] Test asserts the second withdrawal attempt throws.
- [ ] Contract balance assertion passes.
- [ ] Test is isolated and does not depend on other test files.

title: [Testing] Integration test: unauthorized access rejection
body:
## Summary
Verify that the contract correctly rejects unauthorized callers for `withdraw` and `cancel_stream`.

## Implementation Steps
1. Create a stream between `sender` and `recipient`.
2. Attempt to call `withdraw` from a third-party account; assert the transaction fails with an auth error.
3. Attempt to call `cancel_stream` from `recipient` (not the sender); assert the transaction fails.
4. Attempt to call `cancel_stream` from a random third party; assert failure.
5. Verify that the stream state is unchanged after each failed attempt.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] All three unauthorized scenarios are covered by distinct `it` blocks.
- [ ] Each assertion checks both the error type and that stream state is unmodified.
- [ ] Tests run in isolation without shared mutable state.
- [ ] `npm test` exits 0 only when all assertions pass.
